definitions.explanation: Dedicated effort to improve one's knowledge or skills through persistent study and practice. A formal word conveying deep commitment to learning.

examples.japanese: {日々|ひび}{研鑽|けんさん}を{積|つ}む。
examples.english: I pursue continuous self-improvement every day.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}として{研鑽|けんさん}を{怠|おこた}らない。
examples.english: I never neglect my professional development as a doctor.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{研鑽|けんさん}が{実|みの}り、ついに{国際的|こくさいてき}な{賞|しょう}を{受賞|じゅしょう}した。
examples.english: Years of dedicated study bore fruit, and he finally received an international award.

notes:
FORMATION:
{研|けん} (to polish, to sharpen) + {鑽|さん} (to drill into). Both characters convey the idea of persistent, focused effort.

USAGE:
A formal word used in academic, professional, and ceremonial contexts. Common in speeches, resumes, and professional development discussions. Often appears in the set phrase {研鑽|けんさん}を{積|つ}む (to accumulate practice).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {研鑽|けんさん}を{積|つ}む (to pursue continuous improvement)
- {研鑽|けんさん}を{重|かさ}ねる (to build up through practice)
- {研鑽|けんさん}を{怠|おこた}らない (to never neglect self-improvement)
- {自己|じこ}{研鑽|けんさん} (self-improvement, professional development)
